- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak if sentiment >0.8.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases; apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.6.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; add 1–2 days of sentiment-weighted smoothing to forecast horizon.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.1), model often fails to correct; apply 2–5% downward adjustment to next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to overfit short-term volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is erratic (±0.35 or more in 3 consecutive days).
